svg.title: Product direction and the circular seven-outcome software lifecycle
svg.desc: The original layout is preserved: a project baseline above, product direction on the left, seven engineering phase cards arranged in a circular clockwise flow in the centre, product feedback on the right, and shared and technical methods below. Product management remains entirely in Product direction. The software cycle proceeds through requirements engineering, solution design, implementation planning, implementation, verification and testing, release and deployment, and operations and evolution, then repeats based on evidence. Requirements use refine supported by requirements-engineering. Operations include incident response, postmortems, runbooks, reliability, observability, improvement and dependencies in an inset connected to the seventh phase. A central develop label represents an end-to-end engagement. Shared research, documentation, security and review remain cross-cutting; technical examples are capability-oriented rather than specific to Python or any framework. Arrows illustrate dependencies and feedback, not mandatory invocations or authorization to deploy.
